text:
Every request must include a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Tokens are
issued from the dashboard and look like `acme_` followed by 32 hex characters.
heading: Authentication > Tokens

text:
Tokens carry scopes that limit what they can do. The available scopes are `read`,
`write`, and `admin`. A token with only `read` scope receives a 403 response on any
write endpoint. Scopes cannot be changed after a token is created; issue a new token
instead.
heading: Authentication > Scopes

text:
Rotate tokens at least every 90 days. The dashboard keeps the previous token valid for
a 24 hour grace period after rotation so in-flight jobs do not fail. After the grace
period the old token is rejected with a 401 response.
heading: Authentication > Rotation

text:
Install the SDK with pip:

```bash
pip install acme-sdk
```

The SDK requires Python 3.10 or newer. We recommend a virtual environment.
heading: Getting Started > Install

text:
Create a client and make your first request:

```python
from acme import Client
client = Client(token="ACME_TOKEN")
print(client.ping())
```

The `ping` method returns `"pong"` when the API is reachable.
heading: Getting Started > Quickstart

text:
The client reads configuration from environment variables. `ACME_TOKEN` is required;
`ACME_BASE_URL` defaults to `https://api.acme.example`. The default request timeout
is 30 seconds. You can raise it for slow batch jobs by passing `timeout=120` to the
constructor. Configuration values passed to the constructor override environment
variables, which in turn override built-in defaults.
heading: Getting Started > Configuration

text:
The API allows 100 requests per minute per token. Exceeding this returns HTTP 429 with
a `Retry-After` header giving the number of seconds to wait. The SDK retries 429
responses automatically up to three times with exponential backoff.
heading: Troubleshooting > Rate Limits

text:
A 401 means the token is missing, malformed, or expired. A 403 usually means the token
lacks the required scope. A 404 means the resource id does not exist. A 500 is a
server-side fault and is safe to retry.
heading: Troubleshooting > Common Errors

text:
Set `ACME_DEBUG=1` to log every request and response to stderr. Do not enable debug
logging in production because it prints tokens in plaintext.
heading: Troubleshooting > Debugging
